title: Multiple Template Parameters
learningObjectives: Identify template parameters and required operations.
Design a reusable generic utility or type.

understand.concept: Multiple type parameters represent distinct type roles, such as a source type and destination type. Expressions using them must be valid, and conversions may affect the result type.
understand.whyItMatters: Separate parameters make APIs flexible when inputs have different types.
understand.explain: Trace which type each parameter uses and whether the combined expression can be formed. Watch for narrowing and return-type assumptions.

examples.title: Different types
examples.code:
template<class A,class B>auto add(A a,B b){return a+b;}
// add(2,3.5) gives 5.5
examples.explanation: A and B are independently deduced.

examples.title: Two-member record
examples.code:
template<class A,class B>struct Duo{A first;B second;};
Duo<int,double> d{1,2.5};
examples.explanation: Each member uses its own type parameter.

examples.title: Mixed comparison
examples.code:
template<class A,class B>bool same(A a,B b){return a==b;}
// same(4,4.0)
examples.explanation: The comparison expression must be valid for the types.

examples.title: Two-type display
examples.code: template<class A,class B>void show(const A& a,const B& b){std::cout<<a<<b;}

examples.title: Explicit conversion
examples.code:
template<class A,class B>B convert(A v){return static_cast<B>(v);}
int n=convert<double,int>(3.8);

practise.guidedTask: Analyze each Multiple Template Parameters example: identify parameters, requirements, deduced or explicit arguments, and instantiated behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a generic C++ utility or type demonstrating multiple template parameters. Test two supported types, one boundary case, and one unsupported/constrained type; explain why it is or is not accepted.
hints: Begin with a concrete example before generalizing.
Name template parameters for their roles.

questions.explanation: Different parameters can represent different roles.
auto can deduce return expression type.
